tables.label: TABLE 1
tables.caption: Peptides and their amino acid sequences.
footnotes: Underlined amino acids indicate double coupling.
Orn, ornithine; Dab, 2,4-diaminobutyric acid; Dap, 2,3-diaminopropionic acid

tables.label: TABLE 2
tables.caption: Synthesized peptides with their amino acid sequences, expected and observed masses, and the amount of peptide obtained.
footnotes: The expected mass was determined by the CEM, Liberty-blue microwave peptide synthesizer software.
Orn, ornithine; Dab, 2,4-diaminobutyric acid; Dap, 2,3-diaminopropionic acid.
All peptides used in antimicrobial assays are peptide-HCl.

tables.label: TABLE 3
tables.caption: MIC and MBC values for melittin and its analogs toward S. aureus and E. coli.
footnotes: Significantly different (p < 0.05) MIC or MBC, respectively, compared to melittin (native) peptide.

Large effect size (Cohen’s d > 0.8) MIC or MBC, respectively, compared to melittin (native) peptide with b+ indicating a higher and b− indicating a lower MIC or MBC than native melittin, respectively.

tables.label: TABLE 4
tables.caption: LD50, IC50, and HC50 of melittin, melittin dimers, and Lys-substituted melittin toward H4IIE and HEK293 cells and chicken red blood cells (RBCs), respectively.

tables.label: TABLE 5
tables.caption: Therapeutic index for cell lysis, cell proliferation, and hemolysis of H4IIE and HEK293 cells based on the antimicrobial activity of the peptides toward S. aureus.
footnotes: Therapeutic index (TI) determined for cell lysis by LD50/MBC50, for inhibition of proliferation by IC50/MIC50, and hemolysis by HC50/MBC50 (MIC50 and MBC50 of peptides toward S. aureus 29213 used to calculate TI).
